metadata.report_title: Bifacial PV Mounting System Trade-Off Report

site.climate_note: Semi-arid climate with strong summer irradiance and moderate winter diffuse component.

executive_summary: This report compares 2-purlin, 3-purlin and 4-purlin rear-support alternatives for bifacial PV. Results show that lower purlin count improves rear-side gain and energy output, while higher purlin count increases structural confidence and CAPEX. The recommended option balances annual yield advantage with acceptable structure risk and commercial efficiency.
decision_snapshot: The recommended scenario is 2-purlin + brace due to balanced energy and structural profile.
methodology_overview: Monte Carlo rear-side obstruction simulation was used to estimate bifacial shading impact.
NASA POWER and PVGIS climate/albedo context was integrated.
Scenario scoring combines energy, structure confidence and cost normalization.

assumptions.title: Modeling simplification
assumptions.value: Support members are approximated with box geometry for rear-side obstruction analysis.

assumptions.title: Cost baseline
assumptions.value: Base structure CAPEX and purlin uplift assumptions are indicative and project-specific.

scenarios.label: 2-Purlin
engineering_notes: Lower backside shading footprint compared to higher purlin alternatives.

scenarios.label: 2-Purlin + Cross Brace
engineering_notes: Improved frame stiffness and vibration comfort.

scenarios.label: 3-Purlin
engineering_notes: Higher static margin relative to 2-purlin reference.
commercial_notes: Incremental CAPEX uplift requires yield-offset validation.

uncertainty.note: Higher spread due to stronger rear-side obstruction

key_tradeoffs: 2-purlin has better rear-side gain and lower CAPEX but lower structural confidence proxy.
3-purlin improves structural confidence with modest energy penalty and CAPEX increase.
Cross-brace option improves structural behavior but can materially reduce rear-side gain.

recommendation.summary: 3-purlin is recommended for this site profile due to balanced yield retention and stronger structural confidence.
rationale: Energy loss versus 2-purlin remains limited while structure confidence increases materially.
Cost uplift is manageable under current CAPEX assumptions and likely acceptable for EPC risk control.
recommendation.conditional_note: If geotechnical verification confirms low structural risk, 2-purlin can be selected for maximum energy-driven return.
recommendation.investor_takeaway: 3-purlin provides a more bankable risk-return balance for financing discussions.

appendix_notes: Detailed static checks are outside this report scope and should be completed by structural engineering.
Cost assumptions are indicative placeholders and must be updated with procurement quotations.
